nodes.description: Variants alter beta-1 tubulin, the class VI beta-tubulin restricted to the megakaryocyte-platelet lineage and also expressed in thyroid. The p.F260S variant sits at the alpha/beta intradimer interface, and the functional consequence is loss of incorporation rather than a subtle change in dynamics: mutant beta-1 tubulin is not incorporated into microtubules with endogenous alpha-tubulin at all, and alpha-tubulin expression falls in transfected cells. Independently, three thyroid dysgenesis-associated TUBB1 variants were shown to produce non-functional alpha/beta dimers that cannot be incorporated into microtubules - the same failure mode reached from a different phenotype.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous missense variants whose product does not incorporate into microtubules. LOSS_OF_FUNCTION describes the mutant subunit's own activity, which is directly evidenced - it is not incorporated, and the dimers it forms are non-functional. Note this is a different mechanism class from the dominant-negative poisoning resolved for TUBA1A and TUBB8, where the mutant subunit DOES enter the polymer and degrades it from within. Whether the residual haploid dose alone explains the platelet phenotype, or whether sequestration of alpha-tubulin adds a dominant-negative component, is not settled; the observed fall in alpha-tubulin expression in transfected cells is suggestive of the latter.

nodes.description: The second tissue. TUBB1 is expressed in developing and adult thyroid in humans and mice, and Tubb1 knockout in mouse disrupts microtubule integrity by preventing beta-1 tubulin incorporation, impairing thyroid migration and thyroid hormone secretion. In humans, TUBB1 variants co-segregated with thyroid dysgenesis in three families, accounting for 1.1% of a thyroid dysgenesis cohort. This arm is why a TUBB1 result should prompt thyroid assessment rather than being read as a purely haematological finding.

nodes.description: The cellular lesion, and one that is directly visible: in every platelet from affected individuals the circumferential marginal microtubule band is undetectable and the microtubules are frayed and disorganized. In megakaryocytes the same defect diminishes proplatelet formation, producing fewer but larger proplatelet tips - which is exactly the shape of the clinical phenotype, fewer and larger platelets.

nodes.description: A reduced platelet count with abnormally large platelets. Usually mild, often an incidental finding, and readily mistaken for immune thrombocytopenia - which matters, because that misdiagnosis leads to immunosuppressive treatment or splenectomy for a structural, inherited defect.
